content: The ability of semantic reasoning is essential for advanced natural language understanding (NLU) systems. Many NLU tasks that take sentence pairs as input, such as natural language inference (NLI) and machine reading comprehension (MRC), heavily rely on the ability of sophisticated semantic reasoning. For instance, the NLI task aims to determine whether the hypothesis sentence (e.g., a woman is sleeping) can be inferred from the premise sentence (e.g., a woman is talking on the phone). This requires the model to read and understand sentence pairs to make the specific semantic inference.
